performance-suite-seconds.noisePolicy:
One warmup is discarded; three isolated runs are measured; the median must remain at or below the ratcheted maximum.

Raised 21.0 -> 24.0 on 2026-08-14, calibrated from CI rather than from a dev machine. The 21.0 ceiling was set from a dev median of ~19.8s and sat INSIDE the CI distribution: 18 samples across 6 runners over two days ranged 20.352-21.439s (peak-to-peak 5.2%), and observed CI medians included 20.618, 20.692, 21.209 and 22.391s with individual samples to 22.962s. The gate therefore failed on which runner it landed on rather than on any regression, and six controlled same-commit dispatches went 2/3 green on two different branches identically.

24.0 sits ~12% above the highest observed CI sample (21.439s) instead of at roughly the 50th percentile of the distribution. The metric itself is sound and is NOT startup-dominated: startup is 3.8% of the suite on a dev machine and 7.3% on CI, so the measurement is 92-96% compute, and its run-to-run CV (~1.6%) is the lowest of any signal in this suite.

Prior precedent for moving this number with evidence: #942 raised 20.0 -> 21.0, and cut test cost first (one shared index build instead of three) before moving the ceiling. Order matters: cheaper tests first, ceiling second. No test cost was added here, so no such reduction was available.

This ceiling does NOT address #965's runner terminations (exit 143), which are unexplained and are what actually blocked v0.13.2. See docs/plans/performance-gate-strategy.md.
